title: Reddit Plunges 36% Year to Date: Should You Buy the Stock on the Dip?
detail:
Reddit Plunges 36% Year to Date: Should You Buy the Stock on the Dip?
Nilanshi Mukherjee
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 7:59 AM MST
RDDT
PINS
META
SNAP
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Reddit RDDT shares have plunged 35.7% in the year-to-date period, underperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's 24.7% increase. The Zacks Internet - Software industry has also increased 10% in the same time frame.

The company's shares have also underperformed its peers, which include Pinterest PINS, Meta Platforms META and Snap SNAP. These companies are expanding their footprint in the digital advertising market. Shares of Meta Platforms have gained 10.3%, while Pinterest and Snap have lost 25.6% and 30.9%, respectively, in the year-to-date period.

The dip can be explained by irregular and declining search referral traffic, especially toward the end of the second quarter of 2026, causing a slight decrease in the number of daily active users and increasing volatility. The lack of insight into external search trends still poses a problem. Difficult macroeconomic uncertainties and the intense competition in the digital advertising market remain concerns.

RDDT Stock Performance
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Despite these headwinds, Reddit's expanding advertising portfolio, strong user engagement, including rising daily and weekly active users, gains in Average Revenue Per Unique (ARPU) and the expansion of advertiser tools such as Dynamic Product Ads, Reddit Pixel and CAPI have been key catalysts. These factors are helping Reddit to fend off its competitors like Pinterest, Snap and Meta Platforms.

RDDT Benefits From Expanding Portfolio

Reddit's expanding portfolio has been a key catalyst in driving the company's user engagement. In the second quarter of 2026, Reddit reported 130.3 million daily active uniques, up 18% year over year, and 514.6 million weekly active uniques, up 24% year over year.

RDDT is benefiting from successful product innovation and user engagement strategies. The company's focus on improving the experience for new users, particularly through updated feed models and easier posting mechanisms, has led to a 50% year-over-year increase in new app user retention in the second quarter of 2026. Features like video in comments and interactive games have expanded engagement opportunities. At the same time, efforts to convert web users to app users have resulted in higher retention and more valuable user cohorts.

The company's innovation in its ad stack has been a major growth driver. The launch and rapid adoption of Reddit Max, an AI-driven suite for ad automation and optimization, has delivered significant results. Advertiser usage of Max grew more than 60% from the first quarter, and revenues from Max campaigns increased by more than 150%. Features like tailored creatives and dynamic product ads are helping brands achieve better outcomes, such as Lenovo's 40% higher purchase value with Max campaigns compared to standard campaigns.

Further expanding its portfolio, in September 2026, Reddit made its AI-powered Max campaigns available to all advertisers following a beta launch earlier this year. Max campaigns automate targeting, creative selection, placements, and budget allocation while allowing advertisers to retain strategic control. Reddit said early tests delivered 17% lower cost per acquisition and more than 27% higher conversions versus standard campaigns. The company also added Advertising API support, integration with Smartly and new asset groups, enabling advertisers to manage multiple creative sets within a single campaign and assess performance separately.

title: Which Dates Could Move Meta Stock Most?
detail:
Which Dates Could Move Meta Stock Most?
Trefis Team

Image from Pixabay

Meta Platforms (META) stock returned 26% over the past month, against 0.6% for the S&P 500. The rise followed the September 8 launch of Muse, its personal AI agent app. Management has already guided for capital spending of $130 billion to $145 billion in 2026, so each coming report shows whether sales keep pace. Below are the events most likely to move Meta stock over the next six months.

What to watch

	

When

	

Which way it cuts




Meta's third-quarter 2026 results, against its revenue guide of $61 billion to $64 billion

	

Third-quarter 2026 results

	

Either way




Youth-related trials in the U.S., which management said may result in a material loss

	

Before the end of 2026

	

Against the stock




Meta's fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 report, which completes a year of $165 billion to $169 billion in guided expenses

	

Expected on or around January 26, 2027 (fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results)

	

Either way




A judge's ruling on New Mexico's request for up to $40 billion in penalties

	

No date given

	

Against the stock

The First Results Since Muse Launched

Meta's results for the third quarter of 2026 are still to come, and they cover the quarter in which Muse launched. On the July 29, 2026 call, management guided for third-quarter revenue of $61 billion to $64 billion. Meta's sales in the second quarter were $60.8 billion, so the low end of that guide is about level with them.

Almost all of those sales come from ads, which brought in $59.4 billion of the second-quarter total. So while the stock rose in September on a new app, these results will mostly be about the ad business. Revenue above the $64 billion top of the guide would show Meta's sales growing faster than management expected in July.

New Mexico's Penalty Request

New Mexico asked a judge on October 1, 2026, to order Meta to pay up to $40 billion in penalties, Reuters reported. The request followed a jury finding that the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data on Facebook.

The New Mexico case is not the only one. Management said on the July 29 call that youth-related trials are scheduled in the U.S. for 2026 and may result in a material loss.

The New Mexico request is the one with a figure on it. Meta earned $68.1 billion over its last twelve months. It would owe more than half of that profit if the judge orders the full amount.

Meta's January 2027 Earnings Report

Meta is expected to report its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results on or around January 26, 2027, after the market closes. That report completes 2026, a year for which management has raised the lower end of its cost forecast. Management now expects total expenses of $165 billion to $169 billion for 2026. For scale, Meta's revenue over the last twelve months was $228.2 billion.

A poster on reddit's personal finance forum asked a question about his 66-year-old retired mom who wants to move about 40% of her retirement savings into 10-year Treasuries. Her plan is to spend the interest along with Social Security and hold the principal until the bonds mature. The rest of her savings sits in what the poster calls somewhat speculative stocks. A family member talked her into them, and she plans to leave them alone. None of these details are verified.

Andrey_Popov / Shutterstock.com

Her instinct is sound. The plan is closer to right than wrong, but she hasn't accounted for the expensive parts.

What "Locking In" a Treasury Yield Really Means

A 10-year Treasury locks in its yield to maturity only if she holds it to maturity. The bond's market value still moves every day. If she needs the principal early, she sells at whatever buyers will pay. If rates have went up since she bought, that price can be lower than what she paid.

At 66, a 10-year holding period runs into her mid-seventies. So the key question is whether she can leave that principal untouched for the full term. How much she wants the income is secondary.

A 28-year-old has enough money to seriously consider leaving the workforce, but they haven't walked away yet. Their job covers living expenses and provides health insurance, even though they don't enjoy the work.

Now they're trying to decide how many more years, if any, they should keep going.

"Not sure what's next," they shared on Reddit.

Warren Buffett once said, "If you don't find a way to make money while you sleep, you will work until you die." Here's how you can earn passive income with just $100.

The Inheritance Gave Them Options They Hadn't Planned For

The poster wasn't counting on an inheritance. Their family had owned a business that was eventually sold. According to them, the money was "kind of" a surprise.

They now have $2.1 million invested in the S&P 500 and a $650,000 paid-off home. So far, they haven't touched the investments.

"You're in a position where you could teach golf or yoga, work for a nonprofit you care about, go part-time, or take a sabbatical and figure out what you actually want," a commenter said.

The suggestions went beyond finding another job. The original poster could take time off to travel, change careers or find lower-stress work that covers their expenses while the $2.1 million continues growing.

The Bigger Question Was What They Wanted Their Life To Look Like

The OP asked how many more years to work, but hadn't shared how much they spend. They also have no mortgage, spouse or children, so their expenses could look very different in the years ahead.

"What about 10 yrs from now, in a perfect world what would your life look like?" One person asked. "Married and kids? Hobbies? A 'normal' job you actually enjoy? Nomad traveling the world?"

A parent facing a similar situation with their own children offered another perspective. They had asked them not to factor their inheritance into their financial plans until age 35.

"Find a sustainably happy life you're content with and then pile the money on top of that," the commenter said.

title: Reddit Is Growing Above 40% a Year, So Why Is the Stock Down 40%?
detail:
Reddit Is Growing Above 40% a Year, So Why Is the Stock Down 40%?
David Beren
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 5:28 AM MST
RDDT
Trade Reddit on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Reddit Is Growing Above 40% a Year, So Why Is the Stock Down 40%? ©Brett Jordan from Pexels, Karola G from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Reddit closed at $145.35 on September 29, down about 40% this year and roughly 45% below its 52-week high of $263.50.

Second-quarter revenue grew 61% to $805 million at a 43% adjusted EBITDA margin, and consensus expects around 54% revenue growth this year.

TIKR's model shows the P/E multiple down around 38% over the past year while earnings grew, so the drop in the shares comes from a lower multiple.

Third-quarter revenue guidance of $860 million to $870 million sets up the next test of how quickly growth is slowing.

Revenue Growth Is Still Strong but Slowing

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) runs a user-generated content platform that earns money mainly from advertising, plus premium subscriptions and data licensing. Revenue reached $2.2 billion in fiscal 2025, up 69% from $1.3 billion.

In the second quarter, it grew 61% to $805 million, and daily active unique users rose 18% to 130.3 million. The chart below adds consensus estimates through fiscal 2030.

Reddit Revenue Estimates. (TIKR)

Analysts expect revenue near $3.4 billion this year, up around 54%, then around $4.5 billion in fiscal 2027 and around $7.7 billion by fiscal 2030, roughly 3.5 times the fiscal 2025 level.

Growth slows steadily along the way, from around 54% this year to around 32% in fiscal 2027 and around 17% by fiscal 2030. Reddit's own third-quarter guidance is $860 million to $870 million.

Pinterest, another advertising-funded platform built on user content, grew second-quarter revenue 18% at a 26% adjusted EBITDA margin, against 61% and 43% at Reddit.

Profits Are Scaling With the Business

Profits have kept pace with growth. Normalized EPS rose from $2.45 in fiscal 2024 to $4.54 in fiscal 2025, up around 85%, and second-quarter net income was $253 million, or 31% of revenue.

Free cash flow reached $261 million in the quarter, Reddit repurchased $235 million of its stock, and it holds about $2.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. The chart below shows consensus estimates through fiscal 2030.

Reddit EPS Normalized. (TIKR)

Analysts expect EPS of around $7.70 this year, around $9.70 in fiscal 2027, and around $13 by fiscal 2030. This year's earnings are expected to grow around 69% against around 54% for revenue, then slow to around 26% in fiscal 2027.

Estimates barely move between fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029, so the outer years deserve less weight than the near-term figures.

Should You Buy Reddit Stock?

TIKR's valuation model connects growth and margins to a possible return, starting from the September 29 price of $145.35.

Over the past year, it shows the shares down around 28% and the P/E multiple down around 38%. The decline came from a lower multiple, since earnings grew over the same stretch.
